result.builder:
Goal: make one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test that extends packages/jsonl-lint so the CLI accepts several files and stdin, for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104.

Acceptance lines (every one must hold at the PR head):
1. packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before
2. A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)
3. Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)
4. lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged
5. node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage
6. The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

Steps:
1. Read packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md. Today the CLI reads only process.argv[2].
2. Do not edit packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all (not even whitespace); all the change goes in bin/jsonl-lint.js, tests and README.
3. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js (plain ES module, zero dependencies):
   - args = process.argv.slice(2). If empty: write a usage line to stderr (e.g. `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`, mention that - means stdin) and exit 2.
   - If - appears more than once: usage error on stderr, exit 2, before reading anything.
   - For each argument in order: if it is -, read stdin with readFileSync(0, 'utf8'); otherwise readFileSync(file, 'utf8'). If reading fails, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember that a read error happened, and continue with the next file. Otherwise run lint(text) and print `${file}:${line}: ${error with \r?\n replaced by a space}` to stdout for each problem, exactly as the single-file version does, with the prefix being the argument exactly as given (- for stdin).
   - Exit code: 2 if any file could not be read (a read error wins over bad rows), else 1 if any bad row was printed, else 0. Nothing on stdout for clean files.
4. Add node:test tests in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (reuse its spawnSync helper; pass `input` to spawnSync for stdin) covering, each as its own test: two clean files (exit 0, no output); one bad file among several clean ones (exit 1, only that file's lines, in argument order; also a case with two bad files checking their lines appear in argument order); stdin via - clean (exit 0) and bad (exit 1, lines prefixed `-:`); a missing file among good ones (exit 2, message on stderr naming it, and a bad file after the missing one still reported on stdout); two - arguments (exit 2, stderr); no arguments (exit 2, usage on stderr). Keep the existing tests passing.
5. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: Usage shows `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]` (that literal text), explains that files are checked in order, that `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`, that `-` may be given only once, and the new exit codes (0 all clean, 1 any bad row in any file, 2 no file / second `-` / any file unreadable, with other files still checked and reported).
6. Run `npm test` at the repo root and make it pass. Also try by hand: `printf '{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js a.jsonl - b.jsonl` with real files.
7. Commit, push, and open one PR whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) on the PR head to finish; if it fails, fix and push again until it is green.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104 and the harness accepted them. All the verifier's local commands run as written at the current commit. The GitHub check (check 6) couldn't be run here because this session has no GitHub access to the repo (HTTP 403). So that command is in the brief exactly as I wrote and attempted it, but I haven't seen it succeed.

**What the code does today:**
- The CLI only reads the first argument. With four files it checks only the first one, which is clean, so it prints nothing and exits 0.
- `-` is treated as a filename, so it fails with "cannot read -: ENOENT" and exits 2.
- A missing file in the middle of the list is never reached, so it also exits 0.

Each of these fails the matching verifier check, as it should before the change is built. The current 12 package tests pass.

**Builder brief:**
- Rewrite only `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js`: check each argument in order, read `-` from stdin and report it as `-`, and treat a second `-` or no arguments as a usage error (exit 2).
- When a file can't be read, print the error to stderr and keep checking the rest. A read error gives exit 2 even if other files have bad rows.
- Leave `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` untouched.
- Add a `node:test` test for each of the seven cases in the issue, and update the README.
- Open one PR whose body says `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, and wait until the `test` workflow is green.

**Verifier brief:** six checks, one per acceptance line, in order:
1. Several clean and bad files: the output must be each bad file's single-file output, in argument order.
2. stdin through `-`, clean and bad, plus two `-` arguments.
3. Exit codes 0, 1 and 2, including a missing file between good ones, with the error on stderr and the file after it still reported.
4. `src/index.js` must keep the blob hash it has now (`83cbf9f5…`), and `lint` must still give the same output for a sample input.
5. The package tests pass and cover all seven cases, and the README documents the new usage.
6. Exactly one PR with the "Closes" line, its head matches the commit being verified, the `test` check passed, and `npm test` passes.

Extra advice (read errors win over bad rows, error messages still kept to one line) is under a separate "Advisory" heading and doesn't affect pass or fail.
